final.result:
Yes. `go.mod` pins Larkspur v2.0.1, and HTTP/3 support arrived in 2.0.0 according to `sources/CHANGELOG.md`. It's experimental and off by default, so you have to turn it on with `Client{H3: true}` or the `--h3` flag. Before 2.0.0, in the 1.x line, HTTP/3 wasn't supported.

One thing to check: `go.mod` has `require example.com/larkspur v2.0.1` without the `/v2` suffix. Go normally rejects a v2+ version under that path, so it may need to be `example.com/larkspur/v2`, unless the module has no `go.mod` of its own and resolves as `+incompatible`. I haven't built the project, so I haven't confirmed this.
